newsitem.title: USA: DeKalb to buy Custom Farm Seed assets.
newsitem.headline: DeKalb to buy Custom Farm Seed assets.

text.p: DeKalb Genetics Corp said Wednesday it entered into a definitive agreement to purchase certain assets of the Custom Farm Seed (CFS) division of National Starch and Chemical Co.
The deal includes the ongoing commercial CFS seed business. As part of the agreement, DeKalb will purchase the CFS product line as well as a seed conditioning plant in Dwight, Ill.
DeKalb and National Starch also entered into a research collaboration to improve the productivity and functionality of certain starch grains.
The agreement calls for DeKalb to receive royalties for seed products developed through the collaboration and used in National Starch's corn processing facilities.
Terms of the agreements were not disclosed.

National Starch processes waxy and high-amylose corn, both of which are used to produce value-added starch products. The company's CFS division develops, produces and markets seed products, including waxy corn, yellow dent corn, soybeans, and alfalfa.

"CFS is a leader in the waxy corn market, an area of growth for DeKalb," Bruce Bickner, chairman, said in a statement. "We have expanded our lineup of elite waxy hybrids recently, and the CFS purchase will help us better serve this market segment."
